proposals.before: Kerong eventually reached the posts of acting Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
proposals.after: Kerong eventually reached the posts of acting Minister of Works (Sikong) and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
proposals.reason: 司空 is Sikong/Minister of Works among the Three Dukes, not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: Kerong rose in office to acting Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
proposals.after: Kerong rose in office to acting Minister of Works (Sikong) and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
proposals.reason: 司空 is Sikong/Minister of Works, not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: He repeatedly routed the rebel armies, and for his achievements was promoted to Grand Preceptor and advanced to the rank of Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia.
proposals.after: He repeatedly routed the rebel armies, and for his achievements was promoted to Minister of Works (Sikong) and advanced to the rank of Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia.
proposals.reason: 加司空 means promotion to Sikong/Minister of Works, not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: He repeatedly defeated rebel armies; for merit he was made Grand Preceptor and advanced to the Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia rank.
proposals.after: He repeatedly defeated rebel armies; for merit he was made Minister of Works (Sikong) and advanced to the Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia rank.
proposals.reason: 司空 is not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: In the third year of Taihe, After pacifying Cangzhou and Jingzhou he was made Grand Counselor in recognition of his merit and granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.
proposals.after: In the third year of Taihe, after pacifying Cangzhou and Jingzhou he was made Grand Counselor in recognition of his merit and granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.
proposals.reason: Spurious capitalization of After mid-sentence after the reign-year clause.

proposals.before: In the third year of Taihe, He pacified Cang and Jing; for his recorded merit he was made Grand Counselor and granted three hundred households of substantive fief.
proposals.after: In the third year of Taihe, he pacified Cang and Jing; for his recorded merit he was made Grand Counselor and granted three hundred households of substantive fief.
proposals.reason: Spurious capitalization of He after the reign-year clause.

proposals.before: He was soon further honored as Grand Preceptor with privileges equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
proposals.after: He was soon further honored with the prestige rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi (privileges equal to the Three Ducal Ministers).
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is a prestige rank, not the office Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: Soon he was additionally made Grand Preceptor with the same honors as the Three Ducal Ministers.
proposals.after: Soon he was additionally granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi, with the same honors as the Three Ducal Ministers.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is not Grand Preceptor.

proposals.before: Zhongwu eventually reached the posts of Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor.
proposals.after: Zhongwu eventually reached the posts of Minister of Education (Situ) and Grand Counselor.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Situ/Minister of Education, not Grand Mentor (太傅); the idiomatic rendering mistranslates the office.

proposals.before: Zhongwu rose in office to Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
proposals.after: Zhongwu rose in office to Situ (Minister of Education) and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is mistranslated as Grand Mentor; literal English should preserve Situ/Minister of Education.

proposals.before: His son Zhifang — Zhifang — succeeded to his father's position as vice military governor of Youzhou.
proposals.after: His son Zhifang succeeded to his father's position as vice military governor of Youzhou.
proposals.reason: The duplicated Zhifang mirrors a corrupted Chinese repetition and should not be retained in English.

proposals.before: Zhifang was reckless and violent by nature and committed acts of robbery and extortion; for repeated offenses he was demoted to defender of Liuzhou.
proposals.after: Zhifang was reckless and violent by nature and committed acts of robbery and extortion; for repeated offenses he was demoted to Sima of Liuzhou.
proposals.reason: 柳州司馬 is the office of Sima (administrator), not a defender.

proposals.before: Zhifang was by nature reckless and violent and committed acts of forcible seizure; for repeated offenses he was demoted to defender of Liuzhou.
proposals.after: Zhifang was by nature reckless and violent and committed acts of forcible seizure; for repeated offenses he was demoted to Sima of Liuzhou.
proposals.reason: 司馬 should be rendered Sima/administrator, not defender.

proposals.before: In the ninth year of Xiantong, He was further promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.
proposals.after: In the ninth year of Xiantong, he was further promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Situ (Minister of Education), concurrent Grand Mentor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.
proposals.reason: 檢校司徒 is acting Situ, not acting Grand Mentor; 太傅 is Grand Mentor. Also fix the stray capital He.

proposals.before: In the ninth year of Xiantong, He was cumulatively promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.
proposals.after: In the ninth year of Xiantong, he was cumulatively promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Situ, concurrent Grand Mentor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.
proposals.reason: 司徒 and 太傅 are misidentified in the English; 兼太傅 is concurrent Grand Mentor.

proposals.before: In the tenth year, when the people of Xu rebelled, Yunshen asked to send his younger brother Yunguo to lead troops against them, but Emperor Yizong refused.
proposals.after: In the tenth year, when the people of Xu rebelled, Yunshen asked to send his younger brother Yungao to lead troops against them, but Emperor Yizong refused.
proposals.reason: 允臯 is Yungao (臯 gao), not Yunguo; the English given name is a mistranscription.

proposals.before: In the tenth year the people of Xu rebelled; he requested that his younger brother Yunguo lead troops to suppress the rebellion, but Emperor Yizong did not approve.
proposals.after: In the tenth year the people of Xu rebelled; he requested that his younger brother Yungao lead troops to suppress the rebellion, but Emperor Yizong did not approve.
proposals.reason: 允臯 should be romanized Yungao, not Yunguo.

proposals.before: Before long Li Maoxun seized his position. Gongsu returned to the capital and was demoted to registrar of Fuzhou.
proposals.after: Before long Li Maoxun seized his position. Gongsu returned to the capital and was demoted to registrar of Fu Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 復州 is Fu Prefecture (not coastal Fuzhou 福州); the idiomatic rendering 'Fuzhou' invites the wrong place identification.

proposals.before: After the city fell, the Yan army grew somewhat overconfident.
proposals.after: After the city fell, the Yizhou soldiers grew somewhat overconfident.
proposals.reason: Chinese 易州士卒 means the soldiers of/at Yizhou, not a generalized 'Yan army'; the idiomatic gloss invents Yan.

proposals.before: Keju died in the fighting.
proposals.after: Keju died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 可舉死 states only that Keju died; 'in the fighting' is an unsupported addition.

proposals.before: From afar they admired the righteousness of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent times they were infected with the spirit of Lushan and Siming.
proposals.after: From afar they admired the righteousness of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent times they were infected with the spirit of An Lushan and Shi Siming.
proposals.reason: Literal English drops the surnames present in the idiomatic rendering and standard names for 祿山 and 思明, obscuring the referents.

proposals.before: The Li father and son for three generations perished within ten years.
proposals.after: The Li clan, father and sons across three generations, perished within ten years.
proposals.reason: Literal English under-translates 李氏 and makes the three-generation clan-line sense harder to parse.

proposals.before: In the first year of Qianning, in winter Hedong heeded Rengong's plan and marched out to campaign against them.
proposals.after: In the first year of Qianning, in winter Hedong heeded Rengong's plan and marched out to campaign against Yan.
proposals.reason: Literal 'against them' leaves the campaign target unspecified; following 燕軍 supports Yan.

decisions.reason: s0015 檢校司空 is acting Sikong (Minister of Works among the Three Dukes), not Grand Preceptor (太師); the proposed rendering corrects that office.
The same unit's 檢校司空 is Sikong/Minister of Works; literal English likewise cannot read Grand Preceptor.
s0031 以功加司空 awards Sikong for merit, not Grand Preceptor; the replacement matches the Chinese office.
Literal of s0031 likewise has 司空, which is Minister of Works (Sikong), not Grand Preceptor.
After the reign-year clause 太和三年, English mid-sentence "After" is a capitalization error; lowercasing restores ordinary grammar without changing meaning.
Likewise, mid-sentence "He" after 太和三年 is spurious capitalization; the lowercase fix is warranted.
s0038 開府儀同三司 is the prestige rank Kaifu Yitong Sansi (ceremonial equality with the Three Ducal Ministers), not the office Grand Preceptor (太師).
Literal English of the same unit invents Grand Preceptor; Kaifu Yitong Sansi is the correct honor.
s0119 司徒 is Situ/Minister of Education, distinct from Grand Mentor (太傅); the idiomatic must not say Grand Mentor.
Literal of s0119 likewise mistranslates 司徒 as Grand Mentor; Situ (Minister of Education) is required.
Chapter Chinese 子 直方子直方 doubles 直方; Wikisource Jiu Tangshu juan 180 reads 子直方 without the echo, so English should not retain the duplicated name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 子直方，以幽州節度副使襲父位。

decisions.reason: s0124 柳州司馬 is demotion to Sima of Liuzhou; "defender" invents a different office.
Literal likewise must render 司馬 as Sima, not defender.
s0137 檢校司徒 is acting Situ and 兼太傅 is concurrent Grand Mentor; the before swaps those offices (and capitalizes mid-sentence He).
Literal of the same string mislabels 檢校司徒 as acting Grand Mentor and 兼太傅 as concurrent Grand Preceptor; the proposed offices restore the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 檢校司徒、兼太傅、同中書門下平章事

decisions.reason: s0138 允臯 uses 臯 (gāo); Yunguo is a false romanization, and Yungao matches the character.
Literal English must likewise romanize 允臯 as Yungao, not Yunguo.
s0160 復州 is Fu Prefecture, not coastal Fuzhou (福州); "Fu Prefecture" prevents the wrong place identification.
s0176 易州士卒 are the soldiers of Yizhou; "Yan army" invents 燕 and conflicts with the distinct 燕軍 of the next unit.
s0192 is only 可舉死; "in the fighting" adds a manner of death the Chinese does not state.

s0227 literally names 祿山、思明 by given name only; the existing literal mirrors that truncation, while surnames An/Shi are interpretive enrichment already carried in the idiomatic and in the name claims.
s0223 李氏父子三葉 names the Li clan across three generations; omitting 氏 and the clan-line sense under-translates the Chinese.
s0219 出師進討 leaves the target unstated, but the next unit's 燕軍 shows the campaign was against Yan; replacing vague "them" with Yan is supported by that immediate context.

label.en: Grand Preceptor with privileges equal to the Three Ducal Ministers
Kaifu Yitong Sansi (privileges equal to the Three Ducal Ministers)

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0007 shows the English honor label invented Grand Preceptor from a mistranslation of 開府儀同三司; the zh remains correct, so revise the English label to Kaifu Yitong Sansi.
Accepted r0016 establishes that 允臯 is Yungao; the extracted English personal-name Yunguo was created by the bad romanization and must be corrected while zh/pinyin stay.
